question: Critical infrastructure, especially digital infrastructure, has moved considerably higher up the political agenda in recent years. The Strategic Compass paid particular attention to this issue and also proposed that the Commission conduct a risk analysis in 2023 in connection with supply chains for that infrastructure, though the EU has already taken initiatives in this policy area in recent years (Directive (EU) 2022/2557, Directive 2008/114/EC). 1.
How does the risk analysis proposed in the Strategic Compass fit in with the previous initiatives already taken by the EU in this policy area?
Can the Commission say whether that risk analysis has already been completed?
Is not the European Programme for Critical Infrastructure Protection due for a fresh update, given that the security situation has changed particularly significantly since 2006?
answer: There are several initiatives at EU-level to address risks to critical infrastructure, which are coherent with the Strategic Compass for Security and Defence.

In addition to the directive on the resilience of critical entities 2022/2557 (CER Directive) (1), we draw attention of the Honourable Member specifically to the directive 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS-2 Directive) (2). The two Directives are designed in coherence and the NIS-2 Directive is of specific relevance for the resilience of digital infrastructure.

Following up on the Nevers Call of 9 March 2022, cybersecurity risk assessments for communications infrastructure in the EU are being prepared. Among them is a risk assessment on Europe’s communications infrastructures and networks, conducted by Member States with the support of the Commission and ENISA.

Furthermore, in response to repeated calls from Member States and stakeholders, the Commission adopted on 26 February 2024 the recommendation (EU) 2024/779 on Secure and Resilient Submarine Cable Infrastructures (3). The European Programme for Critical Infrastructure Protection (EPCIP) was linked to ECI Directive 2008/114/EC that will be repealed by the CER Directive with effect from 18 October 2024.

The CER Directive is complemented by Council Recommendation of 8 December 2022 on a Union-wide coordinated approach to strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure (4), which includes cooperation on preparedness, response and international cooperation and considers the evolving security situation in Europe.

Directive (EU) 2022/2557 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on the resilience of critical entities, OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 164-198. Directive (EU) 2022/2555 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union, OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80-152.
